The form of surrendering to sensational criticism Korean girl group "BLACKPINK" JENNIE's acting debut "THE IDOL" will end in season 1. On the 28th (local time), according to US media variety, the US HBO series "THE IDOL" reported that the show will end after just one season. HBO said, "'THE IDOL' is one of HBO's most provocative original series. We are happy with the audience reaction. After much discussion and consideration, not only HBO, but the creators and producers have decided not to proceed with Season 2." The TV series, which was unveiled in June this year, is a TV series depicting the world of the music industry and a love story involving popular female pop singers against the backdrop of the music industry in Los Angeles, USA. is. Hollywood star Johnny Depp's daughter Lily-Rose Depp and pop star The Weeknd starred, and JENNIE played Lily-Rose Depp's band in the play. She played Diane, a backup dancer. As JENNIE's first acting challenge, "THE IDOL” could not escape the severe criticism after its release. The sensational performance, lines, and costumes made a big impact. Not only that, but the TV series was also criticized for its sensational, misogynistic, and masculine fantasies. to this, "THE IDOL" was edited from the planned EP6 to all EP5, and the broadcast ended early. On the other hand, BLACKPINK, which JENNIE belongs to, is the largest group among K-POP girl groups with about 1.5 million people. World tour 'BLACKPINK WORLD TOUR 'BORN PINK'' is underway.
